changes: Dotted conversion and validation share safe allocation-free label scanning; C++ allocates only the final returned vector.
Ordinary network input uses safe SliceReader monomorphization in a single bridge invocation, without cursor callbacks or intermediate Vec ownership.
An address-range ownership check selects the callback reader only when input overlaps the C++ cursor object. That path shares the same Rust parser and preserves post-commit label copies.
URL canonicalization writes directly into the eventual C++ std::string. Rust controls BROKEN fallback via callback; no Rust Vec or per-byte Vec push transport remains.
Length readers and conversion functions return scalar validity/length/consumption metadata.
DomainNameLess object disassembly ends in jmp net_dns_names_less, with no byte-span conversion calls or CXX Slice temporaries in this C++ adapter.
Rust comparator assembly retains nonempty raw-slice precondition checks and executes ASCII comparison in Rust.

safety.raw_ffi: Private net_dns_names_less has two documented from_raw_parts sites. Each is limited to a nonempty readable string_view range <= isize::MAX; zero lengths map to &[] without touching the pointer. Inputs can alias; no reference retained or mutation. Public C++ API/export unchanged.
safety.cxx: Shared buffer layout generated by CXX. C++ initializes NameBuffer and LabelChunk before borrowed Rust references. CanonicalName is a stack-only raw_ref to a fresh result std::string.
safety.cursor: The ordinary path borrows disjoint input/output, computes consumed count, ends Rust borrow and commits Skip once. If input bytes overlap any part of the SpanReader object, the same Rust parser uses callback-scoped views and post-commit copied label bytes. No C++ DNS parser or private Rust view of SpanReader exists.
safety.packed_returns: Conversion metadata packs consumed length in the upper 32 bits and output-length-plus-one in the lower 32 bits (zero invalid). DNS limits bound consumption below 448 and output at most 255. Length reads encode width in low two bits and U16 payload length above them, with zero invalid. Policy executes in Rust; C++ only decodes transport.
safety.ownership: Final outputs remain independently owned C++ string/vector/span views according to the existing API; no Rust-owned intermediate Vec is transferred or retained. Aliased length output still commits before reader assignment.

new_tests: CursorInsideLabelPayload: label spanning the entire mutable reader representation, rooted/truncated and both modes.
LengthOutputAliasesCursorSpan: success/failure with output pointing at the reader span subobject.
ComparatorPrefixesAndAliasedViews: long case-folded prefixes, NUL/high bytes, unequal lengths, identical aliases and null-empty views.
